project.name: recitation-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the recitation capability (V9 §18 / §91).
Members (this cut): RecitationMaterialPort (the port), plus the read model and write inputs it carries (MaterialView / MaterialDraft / MaterialFilter).
Why the module exists. Six statements in four files reached into recitation's application layer, across two different consumers and two different deployment units:
agent -> recitation (4) CreateKnowledgeTool, QueryKnowledgeTool, QuizKnowledgeTool, GradeAnswerTool automation -> recitation (2) BlogContentPlanService, BlogPlanRunService
Every one of them imported either recitation.application.RecitationService / KnowledgeQuizService or recitation.api.*. After the split the agent and content-automation services could not be built without recitation's implementation classes.
This cut takes the MATERIALS capability only -- RecitationMaterialPort. It clears automation -> recitation completely (that edge disappears) and halves agent -> recitation, whose remaining two statements are the quiz tools reaching for KnowledgeQuizService. The quiz capability is a second cut: it needs QuizSession, GradedItem, QuizOutcome and the attempt read model, and QuizSession carries a nested list of that read model, so it is a materially larger surface than this one.
Why the filter is NOT recitation.application.RecitationService.MaterialQuery. That nested record's fifth component is an ArchiveFilter -- recitation's own active/archived/all vocabulary. No cross-domain consumer ever names it: both consumers use the four-argument constructor (which defaults the archive dimension to ACTIVE) and the all() factory. So the port takes a four-component filter and the provider maps it onto the four-argument constructor, which lands on exactly the same SQL predicate. Taking the archive dimension across would have been a provider policy the consumers do not participate in, which is precisely what the port-width rule says to leave behind (see docs/migration/adr-contract-boundaries.md §2.6).
Why the DTOs are NARROWED, not mirrored. The mirror rule (§2.5) exists for a type that *replaces* a frontend-visible one: mirroring then makes "serialization is byte-identical" provable, which is what keeps the cut a pure refactor. Nothing here replaces anything. recitation.api.RecitationMaterialView stays exactly where it is and keeps going to the frontend unchanged from recitation.api.RecitationController. MaterialView is new, on a new seam the frontend never sees, so it carries exactly the nine components its consumers read -- id, title, content, knowledgeType, testMode, masteryScore, masteryLevel, reviewCount, nextReviewAt -- out of the view's fourteen. characterCount, lastReviewAt, archivedAt, createdAt and updatedAt have no cross-domain reader. What IS pinned is the component order, by reflection, and the mapping VO -> record, by an app-module test using mutually distinct literals.
Why jakarta.validation annotations are NOT here. recitation.api.CreateRecitationMaterialRequest carries @NotBlank / @Size, and those fire only because RecitationController annotates the parameter @Valid. A contract may not carry them anyway (they would add a dependency, and ADR-1 keeps this module framework-free). Nothing is lost on the agent path, which never had them: the tools build their arguments from JSON, and RecitationService validates the fields itself in validateMaterialRequest. MaterialDraft mirrors the request's four fields without the annotations, and the domain-side request type stays the validated front door for the HTTP callers.
Package note: this module's package is com.xander.lab.recitation.spi, NOT com.xander.lab.recitation.api. recitation already owns com.xander.lab.recitation.api as its *frontend HTTP* layer (CreateRecitationMaterialRequest, RecitationMaterialView, RecitationAttemptView, UpdateRecitationMaterialRequest, KnowledgeQuizAttemptView). Declaring the contract there would put one package in two jars, and would make the scanner classify those controllers as shared kernel, turning "a controller imports its own application layer" into dozens of recitation.api -> recitation backlog edges plus a shared-kernel-reverse-dependency violation each. Same collision as agent-api, automation-api and studio-api; same answer. SHARED_KERNEL lists recitation.spi (dotted, matched longest-first, so it does not swallow recitation.application or recitation.domain).
What is deliberately NOT here yet: - The quiz capability (KnowledgeQuizService: openQuiz / recordQuiz). It is the remaining agent -> recitation pair and the next cut. - Any of recitation's own api layer (com.xander.lab.recitation.api.*). It is the frontend HTTP contract, a different audience, and it joins a contract module only when that layer itself is split in Wave 2.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
